name: Drought
value: El Niño dryness; no harvest failure
summary: El Niño dryness hits eastern Australia's wheat belt; no harvest failure in a major exporter found as of 10 Nov
state: Rainfall across Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria was no more than 25% of normal between 22 Aug and 20 Sep, and Australia's wheat output fell 34% in the last El Niño of 2023–24 (DTN, 23 Sep). ABARES forecast a 12% fall in the 2026–27 wheat area, though heavy carry-in stocks cushion exports (Kpler). Severe drought in a major crop region keeps this at Watch; no harvest failure in a major exporter was found as of 10 Nov.
for_you: Farmers and food importers dependent on Australian wheat and southern African maize are most exposed. Drought in exporting regions tends to feed through to grain and food prices with a lag of months.
rubric_hit: Severe dryness in a major crop region (eastern Australia ≤25% of normal rain): Watch

sources.title: DTN Progressive Farmer — El Niño-related dryness could reduce wheat
Kpler — Ample Australian wheat stocks water down El Niño threat

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
